extra.text: By this the disappearance or concealment of words which are being spoken and such other things are also explained.
extra.note: In Vivekananda's edition, not in this one: the 196th sūtra (etena śabdādy antardhānam uktam).

gap.note: Vivekananda's edition has no counterpart for 4.16 (na caikacittatantraṃ vastu...); his Book 4 has 33 aphorisms, so from 4.17 his numbers run one lower than this edition's.

links.note: Both name practice (abhyāsa) and non-attachment (vairāgya) as the way to master a restless mind.
Vairāgya appears in the Gītā's list of the marks of knowledge, directed at the objects of the senses.
Both join insight (prajñā) to samādhi: the Gītā's person 'steady in wisdom' is 'established in samādhi'.
Both describe a supreme Self distinct from all others, which the Gītā also calls īśvara.
Both use praṇava for the syllable Om; the Gītā calls it what is supreme in all the Vedas.
Both teach repeating Om while holding its meaning, or the Lord, in mind.
The same compound pramāda-ālasya (heedlessness and sloth): obstacles in the Yoga Sūtra, marks of tamas in the Gītā.
Friendliness (maitrī) and compassion (karuṇā), here as attitudes that calm the mind, in the Gītā as marks of the devotee.
The Gītā counts study (svādhyāya) as an austerity (tapas) of speech; the Yoga Sūtra pairs the two in kriyā-yoga.
The same compound guṇa-vṛtti, the working of the three qualities.
Both speak of the seer (draṣṭṛ) who looks on (anupaś-); in the Gītā, the one who sees that only the guṇas act.
Prāṇāyāma: a limb of yoga here, a form of inner offering in the Gītā.
Non-harming (ahiṃsā) and continence (brahmacarya) appear in the Gītā's austerity of the body and among the five yamas here.
Cleanliness (śauca) and austerity (tapas) appear in both lists.
Aparigraha (non-grasping): a yama here, a condition of the solitary yogin in the Gītā.
Both ask for a steady seat, sthiram āsanam.
Prāṇāyāma as the stopping of in- and out-breath here; in the Gītā, the restraint of prāṇa and apāna.
Dhāraṇā: binding the mind to a place here; in the Gītā, yoga-dhāraṇā, the mind held in the heart and the breath at the crown.
One-pointed mind (ekāgra): an outcome of samādhi here, the yogin's starting point on the seat in the Gītā.

kinds.teaching: Same teaching: the two passages say substantially the same thing.
kinds.list: Shared list: both enumerate overlapping items.
kinds.wording: Shared wording: the same word or compound; its sense may differ.

rejected.why: Both use saṃyama, but in the Gītā it is the ordinary verb 'restraining' (the senses), not Patañjali's technical term.
Both use abhijāta, but in the Gītā it means 'born to' (a divine nature), not 'flawless' as of a jewel.
A shared string (pratiṣṭh-) with no shared meaning.

12.13.deva: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी
12.13.iast: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī

14.18.deva: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः
14.18.iast: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ

14.19.deva: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति
14.19.iast: nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati

14.8.deva: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत
14.8.iast: tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata

15.17.deva: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः
15.17.iast: uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ

17.14.deva: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते
17.14.iast: devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate

17.15.deva: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते
17.15.iast: anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate

2.54.deva: स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्
2.54.iast: sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim

4.29.deva: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः
4.29.iast: apāne juhvati prāṇa prāṇe'pānaṃ tathā'pare prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ

6.10.deva: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः
6.10.iast: yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ

6.11.deva: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्
6.11.iast: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram

6.12.deva: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये
6.12.iast: tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye

6.35.deva: असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते
6.35.iast: asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calaṃ abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate

7.8.deva: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु
7.8.iast: raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu

8.12.deva: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्
8.12.iast: sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām

8.13.deva: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्
8.13.iast: omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim

groups.heading: Goal of Concentration
groups.summary: Yoga is the concentration which restricts the fluctuations. Freed from them, the Self attains to self-expression.

groups.heading: Forms of the mind-stuff
groups.summary: The fluctuations are all exposed to attack from the hindrances and are five in number: sources-of-valid-ideas, misconceptions, predicate-relations, sleep, memory.

groups.heading: Methods of restricting fluctuations
groups.summary: An orientation of the whole life with reference to one idea; an emotional transformation corresponding to this focused state.

groups.heading: Kinds of concentration
groups.summary: Four kinds of conscious concentration, and the concentration of subliminal-impressions alone.

groups.heading: Degrees of approach to concentration
groups.summary: The worldly approach; the spiritual approach; the combinations of methods and intensities; and the devotion to the highest Self.

groups.heading: Analysis of the highest Self
groups.summary: Unique quality of the highest Self; proof of His existence; His temporal priority; His symbolical realization.

groups.heading: Obstacles to the calming of the mind-stuff
groups.summary: The inner sense is exposed to distractions which may be overcome by focusing the mind; by the cultivation of sentiments; one may also practise breathings.

groups.heading: Attainment of Stability
groups.summary: Suitable objects for fixed-attention and contemplation.

groups.heading: Mastery and concentration
groups.summary: Classification of concentration with reference to different single objects or absence of objects, or to the mental act, or to a fusion of object and knower.

groups.heading: Normative insight
groups.summary: After-effects of concentrated insight efface after-effects of concentration upon objects.

groups.heading: Devices for weakening hindrances
groups.summary: Aids serviceable to the beginner who is on the path to concentration.

groups.heading: Karma
groups.summary: Origin of karma in hindrances; result of karma in state-of-existence, length of life, and pleasure or pain.

groups.heading: All is pain
groups.summary: Present and future and past correlations with objects result unavoidably in pain.

groups.heading: There is an escape
groups.summary: Only yogins are sensitive to future pain. This may be avoided in that it has not expressed itself in actual suffering.

groups.heading: Cause of pain
groups.summary: The Seer-sight relation: stresses between the aspects, the power of the undefiled Seer, and their correlation until the Seer's purpose is complete.

groups.heading: The escape
groups.summary: Positive state of Isolation follows the ending of the correlation.

groups.heading: Means of escape
groups.summary: The act of discrimination leading up to the act of insight.

groups.heading: Eight aids to yoga
groups.summary: To purify the aspects and to intensify intuitive thinking there are five indirect aids and three direct aids.

groups.heading: First indirect aid: five abstentions
groups.summary: The elements and degrees of morality in the form of prohibitions.

groups.heading: Second indirect aid: five observances
groups.summary: Advances in morality in the form of voluntary action.

groups.heading: Results of the abstentions and observances
groups.summary: Persistent inhibitions of certain kinds reorganize an increase of activity of the opposite kind.

groups.heading: Third indirect aid: postures
groups.summary: Bodily conditions favourable to concentration.

groups.heading: Fourth indirect aid: restraint of the breath
groups.summary: Calming of affective states is favourable to concentration.

groups.heading: Fifth indirect aid: withdrawal of the senses
groups.summary: The span of attention is confined to an inner object.

groups.heading: First direct aid: fixed-attention
groups.summary: The knower focuses the process of knowing upon the object to be known.

groups.heading: Second direct aid: contemplation
groups.summary: A two-term relation between the process of knowing and the object to be known.

groups.heading: Third direct aid: concentration
groups.summary: A fusion of the knower and the process of knowing with the object to be known.

groups.heading: Transition to seedless concentration
groups.summary: The direct aids in combination result in insight and restricted subliminal-impressions and the calm flow of the mind-stuff.

groups.heading: Mutations of substances
groups.summary: In the focused state the concentration holds two time-forms within the span of attention. Mutations are in fixed orders of subliminal-impressions in the restricted state.

groups.heading: Constraint applied to different orders of mutation
groups.summary: Given a single mutation of external-aspect or time-form or intensity, the whole sequence comes under control of the concentrated insight.

groups.heading: Culmination of concentration
groups.summary: The particular which is indiscernible in class or term or point-in-space is intuitively discerned. This is the attainment of Isolation.

groups.heading: Substances and subconsciousness
groups.summary: Correspondence between imperceptible forms of substance and latent-impressions of concentrated states.

groups.heading: Polemic against Idealism
groups.summary: Knowledge of the stream of consciousness is impossible unless it be a permanent order as contrasted with a succession of transient appearances.

groups.heading: Complete Self-realization of the Self
groups.summary: All hindrances subside; all acts of the Self are spontaneous and free.

sutras.en: Now the exposition of yoga [is to be made].
sutras.jn: OM: Here follows Instruction in Union.
sutras.vv: Now concentration is explained.

sutras.en: Yoga is the restriction of the fluctuations of mind-stuff.
sutras.jn: Union, spiritual consciousness, is gained through control of the versatile psychic nature.
sutras.vv: Yoga is restraining the mind-stuff (Chitta) from taking various forms (Vrittis).

sutras.en: Then the Seer [that is, the Self] abides in himself.
sutras.jn: Then the Seer comes to consciousness in his proper nature.
sutras.vv: At that time (the time of concentration) the seer (Purusha) rests in his own (unmodified) state.

sutras.en: At other times it [the Self] takes the same form as the fluctuations [of mind-stuff].
sutras.jn: Heretofore the Seer has been enmeshed in the activities of the psychic nature.
sutras.vv: At other times (other than that of concentration) the seer is identified with the modifications.

sutras.en: The fluctuations are of five kinds and are hindered or unhindered.
sutras.jn: The psychic activities are five; they are either subject or not subject to the five hindrances (Book II, 3).
sutras.vv: There are five classes of modifications, (some) painful and (others) not painful.

sutras.en: Sources-of-valid-ideas and misconceptions and predicate-relations and sleep and memory.
sutras.jn: These activities are: Sound intellection, unsound intellection, predication, sleep, memory.
sutras.vv: (These are) right knowledge, indiscrimination, verbal delusion, sleep, and memory.

sutras.en: Sources-of-valid-ideas are perception and inference and verbal-communication.
sutras.jn: The elements of sound intellection are: direct observation, inductive reason, and trustworthy testimony.
sutras.vv: Direct perception, inference, and competent evidence are proofs.

sutras.en: Misconception is an erroneous idea not based on that form [in respect of which the misconception is entertained].
sutras.jn: Unsound intellection is false understanding, not resting on a perception of the true nature of things.
sutras.vv: Indiscrimination is false knowledge not established in real nature.

sutras.en: The predicate-relation (vikalpa) is without any [corresponding perceptible] object and follows as a result of perception or of words.
sutras.jn: Predication is carried on through words or thoughts not resting on an object perceived.
sutras.vv: Verbal delusion follows from words having no (corresponding) reality.

sutras.en: Sleep is a fluctuation of [mind-stuff] supported by the cause of the [transient] negation [of the waking and the dreaming fluctuations].
sutras.jn: Sleep is the psychic condition which rests on mind states, all material things being absent.
sutras.vv: Sleep is a Vritti which embraces the feeling of voidness.

sutras.en: Memory is not-adding-surreptitiously to a once experienced object.
sutras.jn: Memory is holding to mind-images of things perceived, without modifying them.
sutras.vv: Memory is when the (Vrittis of) perceived subjects do not slip away (and through impressions come back to consciousness).

sutras.en: The restriction of them is by [means] of practice and passionlessness.
sutras.jn: The control of these psychic activities comes through the right use of the will, and through ceasing from self-indulgence.
sutras.vv: Their control is by practice and nonattachment.

sutras.en: Practice is [repeated] exertion to the end that [the mind-stuff] shall have permanence in this [restricted state].
sutras.jn: The right use of the will is the steady, effort to stand in spiritual being.
sutras.vv: Continuous struggle to keep them (the Vrittis) perfectly restrained is practice.

sutras.en: But this [practice] becomes confirmed when it has been cultivated for a long time and uninterruptedly and with earnest attention.
sutras.jn: This becomes a firm resting-place, when followed long, persistently, with earnestness.
sutras.vv: It becomes firmly grounded by long constant efforts with great love (for the end to be attained).

sutras.en: Passionlessness is the consciousness of being master on the part of one who has rid himself of thirst for either seen or revealed objects.
sutras.jn: Ceasing from self-indulgence is conscious mastery over the thirst for sensuous pleasure here or hereafter.
sutras.vv: That effect which comes to these who have given up their thirst after objects, either seen or heard, and which wills to control the objects, is non-attachment.

sutras.en: This [passionlessness] is highest when discernment of the Self results in thirstlessness for qualities [and not merely for objects].
sutras.jn: The consummation of this is freedom from thirst for any mode of psychical activity, through the establishment of the spiritual man.
sutras.vv: That is extreme non-attachment which gives up even the qualities, and comes from the knowledge of (the real nature of) the Purusha.

sutras.en: [Concentration becomes] conscious [of its object] by assuming forms either of deliberation [upon coarse objects] or of reflection upon subtile objects or of joy or of the feeling-of-personality.
sutras.jn: Meditation with an object follows these stages: first, exterior examining, then interior judicial action, then joy, then realization of individual being.
sutras.vv: The concentration called right knowledge is that which is followed by reasoning, discrimination bliss, unqualified egoism.

sutras.en: The other [concentration which is not conscious of objects] consists of subliminal-impressions only [after objects have merged], and follows upon that practice which effects the cessation [of fluctuations].
sutras.jn: After the exercise of the will has stilled the psychic activities, meditation rests only on the fruit of former meditations.
sutras.vv: There is another Samadhi which is attained by the constant practice of cessation of all mental activity, in which the Chitta retains only the unmanifested impressions.

sutras.en: [Concentration not conscious of objects] caused by worldly [means] is the one to which the discarnate attain and to which those [whose bodies] are resolved into primary-matter attain.
sutras.jn: Subjective consciousness arising from a natural cause is possessed by those who have laid aside their bodies and been absorbed into subjective nature.
sutras.vv: (This Samadhi when not followed by extreme non-attachment) becomes the cause of the re-manifestation of the gods and of those that become merged in nature.

sutras.en: [Concentration not conscious of objects,] which follows upon belief [and] energy [and] mindfulness [and] concentration [and] insight, is that to which the others [the yogins] attain.
sutras.jn: For the others, there is spiritual consciousness, led up to by faith, valour, right mindfulness, one-pointedness, perception.
sutras.vv: To others (this Samadhi) comes through faith, energy, memory, concentration, and discrimination of the real.

sutras.en: For the keenly intense, [concentration] is near.
sutras.jn: Spiritual consciousness is nearest to those of keen, intense will.
sutras.vv: Success is speedy for the extremely energetic.

sutras.en: Because [this keenness] is gentle or moderate or keen, there is a [concentration] superior even to this [near kind].
sutras.jn: The will may be weak, or of middle strength, or intense.
sutras.vv: The success of Yogis differs according as the means they adopt are mild, medium, or intense.

sutras.en: Or [concentration] is attained by devotion to the Içvara.
sutras.jn: Or spiritual consciousness may be gained by ardent service of the Master.
sutras.vv: Or by devotion to Ishvara.

sutras.en: Untouched by hindrances or karmas or fruition or by latent-deposits, the Içvara is a special kind of Self.
sutras.jn: The Master is the spiritual man, who is free from hindrances, bondage to works, and the fruition and seed of works.
sutras.vv: Ishvara (the Supreme Ruler) is a special Purusha, untouched by misery, actions, their results, and desires.

sutras.en: In this [Içvara] the germ of the omniscient is at its utmost excellence.
sutras.jn: In the Master is the perfect seed of Omniscience.
sutras.vv: In Him becomes infinite that all-knowingness which in others is (only) a germ.

sutras.en: Teacher of the Primal [Sages] also, forasmuch as [with Him] there is no limitation by time.
sutras.jn: He is the Teacher of all who have gone before, since he is not limited by Time.
sutras.vv: He is the Teacher of even the ancient teachers, being not limited by time.

sutras.en: The word-expressing Him is the Mystic-syllable.
sutras.jn: His word is OM.
sutras.vv: His manifesting word is Om.

sutras.en: Repetition of it and reflection upon its meaning [should be made].
sutras.jn: Let there be soundless repetition of OM and meditation thereon.
sutras.vv: The repetition of this (Om) and meditating on its meaning (is the way).

sutras.en: Thereafter comes the right-knowledge of him who thinks in an inverse way, and the removal of obstacles.
sutras.jn: Thence come the awakening of interior consciousness, and the removal of barriers.
sutras.vv: From that is gained (the knowledge of) introspection, and the destruction of obstacles.

sutras.en: Sickness and languor and doubt and heedlessness and worldliness and erroneous perception and failure to attain any stage [of concentration] and instability in the state [when attained] — these distractions of the mind-stuff are the obstacles.
sutras.jn: The barriers to interior consciousness, which drive the psychic nature this way and that, are these: sickness, inertia, doubt, lightmindedness, laziness, intemperance, false notions, inability to reach a stage of meditation, or to hold it when reached.
sutras.vv: Disease, mental laziness, doubt, lack of enthusiasm, lethargy, clinging to sense-enjoyments, false perception, non-attaining concentration, and falling away from the state when obtained, are the obstructing distractions.

sutras.en: Pain and despondency and unsteadiness of the body and inspiration and expiration are the accompaniments of the distractions.
sutras.jn: Grieving, despondency, bodily restlessness, the drawing in and sending forth of the life-breath also contribute to drive the psychic nature to and fro.
sutras.vv: Grief, mental distress, tremor of the body, irregular breathing, accompany non-retention of concentration.

sutras.en: To check them [let there be] practice upon a single entity.
sutras.jn: Steady application to a principle is the way to put a stop to these.
sutras.vv: To remedy this, the practice of one subject (should be made).

sutras.en: By the cultivation of friendliness towards happiness, and compassion towards pain, and joy towards merit, and indifference towards demerit.
sutras.jn: By sympathy with the happy, compassion for the sorrowful, delight in the holy, disregard of the unholy, the psychic nature moves to gracious peace.
sutras.vv: Friendship, mercy, gladness, and indifference, being thought of in regard to subjects, happy, unhappy, good, and evil respectively, pacify the Chitta.

sutras.en: Or [the yogin attains the undisturbed calm of the mind-stuff] by expulsion and retention of breath.
sutras.jn: Or peace may be reached by the even sending forth and control of the life-breath.
sutras.vv: By throwing out and restraining the Breath.

sutras.iast: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī
sutras.en: Or [he gains stability when] a sense-activity arises connected with an object [and] bringing the central-organ into a relation of stability.
sutras.jn: Faithful, persistent application to any object, if completely attained, will bind the mind to steadiness.
sutras.vv: Those forms of concentration that bring extraordinary sense-perceptions cause perseverance of the mind.

sutras.en: Or an undistressed [and] luminous [sense-activity when arisen brings the central-organ into a relation of stability].
sutras.jn: As also will a joyful, radiant spirit.
sutras.vv: Or (by the meditation on) the Effulgent Light, which is beyond all sorrow.

sutras.en: Or the mind-stuff [reaches the stable state] by having as its object [a mind-stuff] freed from passion.
sutras.jn: Or the purging of self-indulgence from the psychic nature.
sutras.vv: Or (by meditation on) the heart that has given up all attachment to sense-objects.

sutras.en: Or [the mind-stuff reaches the stable state] by having as the supporting-object a perception in dream or in sleep.
sutras.jn: Or a pondering on the perceptions gained in dreams and dreamless sleep.
sutras.vv: Or by meditating on the knowledge that comes in sleep.

sutras.en: Or [the mind-stuff reaches the stable state] by contemplation upon any such an object as is desired.
sutras.jn: Or meditative brooding on what is dearest to the heart.
sutras.vv: Or by the meditation on anything that appeals to one as good.

sutras.en: His mastery extends from the smallest atom to the greatest magnitude.
sutras.jn: Thus he masters all, from the atom to the Infinite.
sutras.vv: The Yogi's mind thus meditating, becomes unobstructed from the atomic to the infinite.

sutras.iast: kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā samāpattiḥ
sutras.en: [The mind-stuff] from which, as from a precious gem, fluctuations have dwindled away, reaches the balanced-state, which, in the case of the knower or of the process-of-knowing or of the object-to-be-known, is in the state of resting upon [one] of these [three] and in the state of being tinged by [one] of these [three].
sutras.jn: When the perturbations of the psychic nature have all been stilled, then the consciousness, like a pure crystal, takes the colour of what it rests on, whether that be the perceiver, perceiving, or the thing perceived.
sutras.vv: The Yogi whose Vrittis have thus become powerless (controlled) obtains in the receiver, (the instrument of) receiving, and the received (the Self, the mind, and external objects), concentratedness arid sameness like the crystal (before different coloured objects).
sutras.vvnote: Printed 'concentratedness arid sameness'; 'arid' is a misprint for 'and' in the source text.

sutras.en: Of [these balanced-states] the state-balanced with deliberation is confused by reason of predicate-relations between words and intended-objects and ideas.
sutras.jn: When the consciousness, poised in perceiving, blends together the name, the object dwelt on and the idea, this is perception with exterior consideration.
sutras.vv: Sound, meaning, and resulting knowledge, being mixed up, is (called) Samadhi with question.

sutras.en: When the memory is quite purified, [that balanced-state] — which is, as it were, empty of itself and which brightens [into conscious knowledge] as the intended-object and nothing more — is super-deliberative.
sutras.jn: When the object dwells in the mind, clear of memory-pictures, uncoloured by the mind, as a pure luminous idea, this is perception without exterior or consideration.
sutras.vv: The Samadhi called "without question" (comes) when the memory is purified, or devoid of qualities, expressing only the meaning (of the meditated object).

sutras.iast: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā
sutras.deva: एतयैव सविचारा निर्विचारा च सूक्ष्मविषया व्याख्याता
sutras.en: By this same [balanced-state] the reflective and the super-reflective [balanced-states] are also explained.
sutras.jn: The same two steps, when referring to things of finer substance, are said to be with, or without, judicial action of the mind.
sutras.vv: By this process (the concentrations) with discrimination and without discrimination, whose objects are finer, are (also) explained.

sutras.en: The subtile object also terminates in unresoluble-primary-matter (aliṅga).
sutras.jn: Subtle substance rises in ascending degrees, to that pure nature which has no distinguishing mark.
sutras.vv: The finer objects end with the Pradhâna.

sutras.en: These same [balanced-states] are the seeded concentration.
sutras.jn: The above are the degrees of limited and conditioned spiritual consciousness, still containing the seed of separateness.
sutras.vv: These concentrations are with seed.

sutras.en: When there is the clearness of the super-reflective [balanced-state, the yogin gains] internal undisturbed calm.
sutras.jn: When pure perception without judicial action of the mind is reached, there follows the gracious peace of the inner self.
sutras.vv: The concentration "without discrimination" being purified, the Chitta becomes firmly fixed.

sutras.en: In this [concentrated mind-stuff] the insight is truth-bearing.
sutras.jn: In that peace, perception is unfailingly true.
sutras.vv: The knowledge in that is called "filled with Truth".

sutras.en: Has another object than the insight resulting from things heard or from inferences, inasmuch as its intended-object is a particular.
sutras.jn: The object of this perception is other than what is learned from the sacred books, or by sound inference, since this perception is particular.
sutras.vv: The knowledge that is gained from testimony and inference is about common objects. That from the Samadhi just mentioned is of a much higher order, being able to penetrate where inference and testimony cannot go.

sutras.en: The subliminal-impression produced by this [super-reflective balanced-state] is hostile to other subliminal-impressions.
sutras.jn: The impress on the consciousness springing from this perception supersedes all previous impressions.
sutras.vv: The resulting impression from this Samadhi obstructs all other impressions.

sutras.en: When this [subliminal-impression] also is restricted, since all is restricted, [the yogin gains] seedless concentration.
sutras.jn: When this impression ceases, then, since all impressions have ceased, there arises pure spiritual consciousness, with no seed of separateness left.
sutras.vv: By the restraint of even this (impression, which obstructs all other impressions), all being restrained, comes the "seedless" Samadhi.

sutras.en: Self-castigation and study and devotion to the Içvara are the Yoga of action.
sutras.jn: The practices which make for union with the Soul are: fervent aspiration, spiritual reading, and complete obedience to the Master.
sutras.vv: Mortification, study, and surrendering fruits of work to God are called Kriyâ-yoga.

sutras.en: For the cultivation of concentration and for the attenuation of the hindrances.
sutras.jn: Their aim is, to bring soul-vision, and to wear away hindrances.
sutras.vv: (It is for) the practice of Samadhi and minimising the pain-bearing obstructions.

sutras.en: Undifferentiated-consciousness (avidyā) and the feeling-of-personality and passion and aversion and the will-to-live are the five hindrances.
sutras.jn: These are the hindrances: the darkness of unwisdom, self-assertion, lust hate, attachment.
sutras.vv: The pain-bearing obstructions are — ignorance, egoism, attachment, aversion and clinging to life.

sutras.en: Undifferentiated-consciousness is the field for the others whether they be dormant or attenuated or intercepted or sustained.
sutras.jn: The darkness of unwisdom is the field of the others. These hindrances may be dormant, or worn thin, or suspended, or expanded.
sutras.vv: Ignorance is the productive field of all these that follow, whether they are dormant, attenuated, overpowered, or expanded.

sutras.en: The recognition of the permanent, of the pure, of pleasure, and of a self in what is impermanent, impure, pain, and not-self is undifferentiated-consciousness (avidyā).
sutras.jn: The darkness of ignorance is: holding that which is unenduring, impure, full of pain, not the Soul, to be eternal, pure, full of joy, the Soul.
sutras.vv: Ignorance is taking the non-eternal, the impure, the painful, and the non-Self for the eternal, the pure, the happy, and the Âtman or Self (respectively).

sutras.en: When the power of seeing and the power by which one sees have the appearance of being a single self, [this is] the feeling-of-personality.
sutras.jn: Self-assertion comes from thinking of the Seer and the instrument of vision as forming one self.
sutras.vv: Egoism is the identification of the seer with the instrument of seeing.

sutras.en: Passion is that which dwells upon pleasure.
sutras.jn: Lust is the resting in the sense of enjoyment.
sutras.vv: Attachment is that which dwells on pleasure.

sutras.en: Aversion is that which dwells upon pain.
sutras.jn: Hate is the resting in the sense of pain.
sutras.vv: Aversion is that which dwells on pain.

sutras.deva: स्वरसवाही विदुषो ऽपि तथा रूढो ऽभिनिवेशः
sutras.en: The will-to-live sweeping on [by the force of] its own nature exists in this form even in the wise.
sutras.jn: Attachment is the desire toward life, even in the wise, carried forward by its own energy.
sutras.vv: Flowing through its own nature, and established even in the learned, is the clinging to life.

sutras.en: These [hindrances when they have become subtile] are to be escaped by the inverse-propagation.
sutras.jn: These hindrances, when they have become subtle, are to be removed by a countercurrent.
sutras.vv: The fine Samskaras are to be conquered by resolving them into their causal state.

sutras.en: The fluctuations of these should be escaped by means of contemplation.
sutras.jn: Their active turnings are to be removed by meditation.
sutras.vv: By meditation, their (gross) modifications are to be rejected.

sutras.en: The latent-deposit of karma has its root in the hindrances and may be felt in a birth seen or in a birth unseen.
sutras.jn: The burden of bondage to sorrow has its root in these hindrances. It will be felt in this life, or in a life not yet manifested.
sutras.vv: The "receptacle of works" has its root in these pain-bearing obstructions, and their experience is in this visible life, or in the unseen life.

sutras.en: So long as the root exists, there will be fruition from it [that is] birth [and] length-of-life [and] kind-of-experience.
sutras.jn: From this root there grow and ripen the fruits of birth, of the life-span, of all that is tasted in life.
sutras.vv: The root being there, the fruition comes (in the form of) species, life, and experience of pleasure and pain.

sutras.en: These [fruitions] have joy or extreme anguish as results in accordance with the quality of their causes whether merit or demerit.
sutras.jn: These bear fruits of rejoicing, or of affliction, as they are sprung from holy or unholy works.
sutras.vv: They bear fruit as pleasure or pain, caused by virtue or vice.

sutras.iast: pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhair guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ
sutras.en: As being the pains which are mutations and anxieties and subliminal-impressions, and by reason of the opposition of the fluctuations of the aspects (guṇa), — to the discriminating all is nothing but pain.
sutras.jn: To him who possesses discernment, all personal life is misery, because it ever waxes and wanes, is ever afflicted with restlessness, makes ever new dynamic impresses in the mind; and because all its activities war with each other.
sutras.vv: To the discriminating, all is, as it were, painful on account of everything bringing pain either as consequence, or as anticipation of loss of happiness, or as fresh craving arising from impressions of happiness, and also as counteraction of qualities.

sutras.en: That which is to be escaped is pain yet to come.
sutras.jn: This pain is to be warded off, before it has come.
sutras.vv: The misery which is not yet come is to be avoided.

sutras.en: The correlation of the Seer and the object-of-sight is the cause of that which is to be escaped.
sutras.jn: The cause of what is to be warded off, is the absorption of the Seer in things seen.
sutras.vv: The cause of that which is to be avoided is the junction of the seer and the seen.

sutras.en: With a disposition to brightness and to activity and to inertia, and with the elements and the organs as its essence, and with its purpose the experience and the liberation [of the Self], — this is the object-of-sight.
sutras.jn: Things seen have as their property manifestation, action, inertia. They form the basis of the elements and the sense-powers. They make for experience and for liberation.
sutras.vv: The experienced is composed of elements and organs, is of the nature of illumination, action, and inertia, and is for the purpose of experience and release (of the experiencer).

sutras.en: The particularized and the unparticularized [forms] and the resoluble only [into primary matter] and irresoluble-primary-matter — are the divisions of the aspects (guṇa).
sutras.jn: The grades or layers of the Three Potencies are the defined, the undefined, that with distinctive mark, that without distinctive mark.
sutras.vv: The states of the qualities are the defined, the undefined, the indicated only, and the signless.

sutras.en: The Seer who is nothing but [the power of seeing], although undefiled (çuddha), looks upon the presented idea.
sutras.jn: The Seer is pure vision. Though pure, he looks out through the vesture of the mind.
sutras.vv: The seer is intelligence only, and though pure, sees through the colouring of the intellect.

sutras.en: The object-of-sight is only for the sake of it [the Self].
sutras.jn: The very essence of things seen is, that they exist for the Seer.
sutras.vv: The nature of the experienced is for him.

sutras.iast: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt
sutras.en: Though it has ceased [to be seen] in the case of one whose purpose is accomplished, it has not ceased to be, since it is common to others [besides himself].
sutras.jn: Though fallen away from him who has reached the goal, things seen have not alto fallen away, since they still exist for others.
sutras.vv: Though destroyed for him whose goal has been gained, yet it is not destroyed, being common to others.

sutras.en: The reason for the apperception of what the power of the property and of what the power of the proprietor are, is correlation.
sutras.jn: The association of the Seer with things seen is the cause of the realizing of the nature of things seen, and also of the realizing of the nature of the Seer.
sutras.vv: Junction is the cause of the realization of the nature of both the powers, the experienced and its Lord.

sutras.en: The reason for this [correlation] is undifferentiated-consciousness (avidyā).
sutras.jn: The cause of this association is the darkness of unwisdom.
sutras.vv: Ignorance is its cause.

sutras.en: Since this [non-sight] does not exist, there is no correlation. This is the escape, the Isolation of the Seer.
sutras.jn: The bringing of this association to an end, by bringing the darkness of unwisdom to an end, is the great liberation; this is the Seer’s attainment of his own pure being.
sutras.vv: There being absence of that (ignorance) there is absence of junction, which is the thing-to-be avoided; that is the independence of the seer.

sutras.en: The means of attaining escape is unwavering discriminative discernment.
sutras.jn: A discerning which is carried on without wavering is the means of liberation.
sutras.vv: The means of destruction of ignorance is unbroken practice of discrimination.

sutras.en: For him [there is] insight sevenfold and advancing in stages to the highest.
sutras.jn: His illuminations is sevenfold, rising In successive stages.
sutras.vv: His knowledge is of the sevenfold highest ground.

sutras.en: After the aids to yoga have been followed up, when the impurity has dwindled, there is an enlightenment of perception reaching up to the discriminative discernment.
sutras.jn: From steadfastly following after the means of Yoga, until impurity is worn away, there comes the illumination of thought up to full discernment.
sutras.vv: By the practice of the different parts of Yoga the impurities being destroyed, knowledge becomes effulgent up to discrimination.

sutras.en: Abstentions and observances and postures and regulations-of-the-breath and withdrawal-of-the-senses and fixed-attention and contemplation and concentration.
sutras.jn: The eight means of Yoga are: the Commandments, the Rules, right Poise, right Control of the life-force, Withdrawal, Attention, Meditation, Contemplation.
sutras.vv: Yama, Niyama, Âsana, Prânâyâama, Pratyâhâra, Dhâranâ, Dhyâna, and Samâdhi are the eight limbs of Yoga.

sutras.en: Abstinence from injury and from falsehood and from theft and from incontinence and from acceptance of gifts are the abstentions.
sutras.jn: The Commandments are these: nom injury, truthfulness, abstaining from stealing, from impurity, from covetousness.
sutras.vv: Non-killing, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, and nor-receiving are called Yamas.

sutras.en: When they are unqualified by species or place or time or exigency and when [covering] all [these] classes — there is the Great Course-of-conduct.
sutras.jn: The Commandments, not limited to any race, place, time or occasion, universal, are the great obligation.
sutras.vv: These, unbroken by time, place, purpose, and caste-rules, are (universal) great vows.

sutras.en: Cleanliness and contentment and self-castigation and study and devotion to the Içvara are the observances.
sutras.jn: The Rules are these: purity, serenity fervent aspiration, spiritual reading, and per feet obedience to the Master.
sutras.vv: Internal and external purification, contentment, mortification, study, and worship of God are the Niyamas.

sutras.en: If there be inhibition by perverse-considerations, there should be cultivation of the opposites.
sutras.jn: When transgressions hinder, the weight of the imagination should be thrown’ on the opposite side.
sutras.vv: To obstruct thoughts which are inimical to Yoga, contrary thoughts should be brought.

sutras.iast: vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam
sutras.deva: वितर्का हिंसादयः कृतकारितानुमोदिता लोभक्रोधमोहपूर्वका मृदुमध्याधिमात्रा दुःखाज्ञानानन्तफला इति प्रतिपक्षभावनम्
sutras.en: Since perverse-considerations such as injuries, whether done or caused to be done or approved, whether ensuing upon greed or anger or infatuation, whether mild or moderate or vehement, find their unending consequences in pain and lack of thinking, there should be the cultivation of their opposites.
sutras.jn: Transgressions are injury, falsehood, theft, incontinence, envy; whether committed, or caused, or assented to, through greed, wrath, or infatuation; whether faint, or middling, or excessive; bearing endless, fruit of ignorance and pain. Therefore must the weight be cast on the other side.
sutras.vv: The obstructions to Yoga are killing, falsehood, etc., whether committed, caused, or approved; either through avarice, or anger, or ignorance; whether slight, middling, or great; and they result in infinite ignorance and misery. This is (the method of) thinking the contrary.

sutras.en: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from injury, his presence begets a suspension of enmity.
sutras.jn: Where non-injury is perfected, all enmity ceases in the presence of him who possesses it.
sutras.vv: Non-killing being established, in his presence all enmities cease (in others).

sutras.en: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from falsehood, actions and consequences depend upon him.
sutras.jn: When he is perfected in truth, all acts and their fruits depend on him.
sutras.vv: By the establishment of truthfulness the Yogi gets the power of attaining for himself and others the fruits of work without the works.

sutras.en: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from theft, all jewels approach him.
sutras.jn: Where cessation from theft is perfected, all treasures present themselves to him who possesses it.
sutras.vv: By the establishment of non-stealing all wealth comes to the Yogi.

sutras.en: As soon as he is grounded in abstinence from incontinence, he acquires energy.
sutras.jn: For him who is perfect in continence, the reward is valour and virility.
sutras.vv: By the establishment of continence energy is gained.

sutras.en: As soon as he is established in abstinence from acceptance of gifts, a thorough illumination upon the conditions of birth.
sutras.jn: Where there is firm conquest of covetousness, he who has conquered it awakes to the how and why of life.
sutras.vv: When he is fixed in non-receiving, he gets the memory of past life.

sutras.en: As a result of cleanliness there is disgust at one's own body and no intercourse with others.
sutras.jn: Through purity a withdrawal from one’s own bodily life, a ceasing from infatuation with the bodily life of others.
sutras.vv: Internal and external cleanliness being established, there arises disgust for one's own body, and non-intercourse with others.

sutras.en: Purity of sattva and gentleness and singleness-of-intent and subjugation of the senses and fitness for the sight of the self.
sutras.jn: To the pure of heart come also a quiet spirit, one-pointed thought, the victory over sensuality, and fitness to behold the Soul.
sutras.vv: There also arises purification of the Sattva, cheerfulness of the mind, concentration, conquest of the organs, and fitness for the realisation of the Self.

sutras.en: As a result of contentment there is an acquisition of superlative pleasure.
sutras.jn: From acceptance, the disciple gains happiness supreme.
sutras.vv: From contentment comes superlative happiness.

sutras.en: Perfection in the body and in the organs after impurity has dwindled as a result of self-castigation.
sutras.jn: The perfection of the powers of the bodily vesture comes through the wearing away of impurities, and through fervent aspiration.
sutras.vv: The result of mortification is bringing powers to the organs and the body, by destroying the impurity.

sutras.en: As a result of study there is communion with the chosen deity.
sutras.jn: Through spiritual reading, the disciple gains communion with the divine Power on which his heart is set.
sutras.vv: By the repetition of the Mantra comes the realisation of the intended deity.

sutras.en: Perfection of concentration as a result of devotion to the Içvara.
sutras.jn: Soul-vision is perfected through perfect obedience to the Master.
sutras.vv: By sacrificing all to Ishvara comes Samadhi.

sutras.en: Stable-and-easy posture.
sutras.jn: Right poise must be firm and without strain.
sutras.vv: Posture is that which is firm and pleasant.

sutras.en: By relaxation of effort or by a [mental] state-of-balance with reference to Ananta.
sutras.jn: Right poise is to be gained by steady and temperate effort, and by setting the heart upon the everlasting.
sutras.vv: By lessening the natural tendency (for restlessness) and meditating on the unlimited, posture becomes firm and pleasant.

sutras.en: Thereafter he is unassailed by extremes.
sutras.jn: The fruit of right poise is the strength to resist the shocks of infatuation or sorrow.
sutras.vv: Seat being conquered, the dualities do not obstruct.

sutras.en: When there is [stability of posture], the restraint of breath, a cutting off of the flow of inspiration and expiration, follows.
sutras.jn: When this is gained, there follows the right guidance of the life-currents, the control of the incoming and outgoing breath.
sutras.vv: Controlling the motion of the exhalation and the inhalation follows after this.

sutras.en: [This is] external or internal or suppressed in fluctuation and is regulated by place and time and number and is protracted and subtile.
sutras.jn: The life-current is either outward, or inward, or balanced; it is regulated according to place, time, number; it is prolonged and subtle.
sutras.vv: Its modifications are either external or internal, or motionless, regulated by place, time, and number, either long or short.

sutras.en: The fourth [restraint of the breath] transcends the external and the internal object.
sutras.jn: The fourth degree transcends external and internal objects.
sutras.vv: The fourth is restraining the Prana by reflecting on external or internal object.

sutras.en: As a result of this the covering of the light dwindles away.
sutras.jn: Thereby is worn away the veil which covers up the light.
sutras.vv: From that, the covering to the light of the Chitta is attenuated.

sutras.en: For fixed-attentions also the central organ becomes fit.
sutras.jn: Thence comes the mind’s power to hold itself in the light.
sutras.vv: The mind becomes fit for Dharana.

sutras.en: The withdrawal of the senses is as it were the imitation of the mind-stuff as it is in itself on the part of the organs by disjoining themselves from their object.
sutras.jn: The right Withdrawal is the disengaging of the powers from entanglement in outer things, as the psychic nature has been withdrawn and stilled.
sutras.vv: The drawing in of the organs is by their giving up their own objects and taking the form of the mind-stuff, as it were.

sutras.en: As a result of this [withdrawal] there is a complete-mastery of the organs.
sutras.jn: Thereupon follows perfect mastery over the powers.
sutras.vv: Thence arises supreme control of the organs.

sutras.en: Binding the mind-stuff to a place is fixed-attention.
sutras.jn: The binding of the perceiving consciousness to a certain region is attention (dharana).
sutras.vv: Dhâranâ is holding the mind on to some particular object.

sutras.en: Focusedness of the presented idea upon that [place] is contemplation.
sutras.jn: A prolonged holding of the perceiving consciousness in that region is meditation (dhyana).
sutras.vv: An unbroken flow of knowledge in that object is Dhyâna.

sutras.en: This same [contemplation], shining forth [in consciousness] as the intended object and nothing more, and, as it were, emptied of itself, is concentration.
sutras.jn: When the perceiving consciousness in this meditative is wholly given to illuminating the essential meaning of the object contemplated, and is freed from the sense of separateness and personality, this is contemplation (samadhi).
sutras.vv: When that, giving up all forms, reflects only the meaning, it is Samâdhi.
sutras.jnote: Gutenberg prints “in this meditative”; a word, probably “state”, appears to be missing.

sutras.en: The three in one are constraint.
sutras.jn: When these three, Attention, Meditation Contemplation, are exercised at once, this is perfectly concentrated Meditation (sanyama).
sutras.vv: (These) three (when practiced) in regard to one object is Samyama.

sutras.en: As a result of mastering this constraint, there follows the shining forth of insight.
sutras.jn: By mastering this perfectly concentrated Meditation, there comes the illumination of perception.
sutras.vv: By the conquest of that comes light of knowledge.

sutras.en: Its application is by stages.
sutras.jn: This power is distributed in ascending degrees.
sutras.vv: That should be employed in stages.

sutras.en: The three are direct aids in comparison with the previous [five].
sutras.jn: This threefold power, of Attention, Meditation, Contemplation, is more interior than the means of growth previously described.
sutras.vv: These three are more internal than those that precede.

sutras.en: Even these [three] are indirect aids to seedless [concentration].
sutras.jn: But this triad is still exterior to the soul vision which is unconditioned, free from the seed of mental analyses.
sutras.vv: But even they are external to the seedless (Samadhi).

sutras.en: When there is a becoming invisible of the subliminal-impression of emergence and a becoming visible of the subliminal-impression of restriction, the mutation of restriction is inseparably connected with mind-stuff in its period of restriction.
sutras.jn: One of the ascending degrees is the development of Control. First there is the overcoming of the mind-impress of excitation. Then comes the manifestation of the mind-impress of Control. Then the perceiving consciousness follows after the moment of Control.
sutras.vv: By the suppression of the disturbed impressions of the mind, and by the rise of impressions of control, the mind, which persists in that moment of control, is said to attain the controlling modifications.

sutras.en: This [mind-stuff] flows peacefully by reason of the subliminal-impression.
sutras.jn: Through frequent repetition of this process, the mind becomes habituated to it, and there arises an equable flow of perceiving consciousness.
sutras.vv: Its flow becomes steady by habit.

sutras.en: The mutation of concentration is the dwindling of dispersiveness and the uprisal of singleness-of-intent belonging to the mind-stuff.
sutras.jn: The gradual conquest of the mind’s tendency to flit from one object to another, and the power of one-pointedness, make the development of Contemplation.
sutras.vv: Taking in all sorts of objects, and concentrating upon one object, these two powers being destroyed and manifested respectively, the Chitta gets the modification called Samadhi.

sutras.en: Then again when the quiescent and the uprisen presented-ideas are similar [in respect of having a single object], the mind-stuff has a mutation single-in-intent.
sutras.jn: When, following this, the controlled manifold tendency and the aroused one-pointedness are equally balanced parts of the perceiving consciousness, his the development of one-pointedness.
sutras.vv: The one-pointedness of the Chitta is when the impression that is past and that which is present are similar.

sutras.en: Thus with regard to elements and to organs, mutations of external-aspect and of time-variation and of intensity have been enumerated.
sutras.jn: Through this, the inherent character, distinctive marks and conditions of being and powers, according to their development, are made clear.
sutras.vv: By this is explained the threefold transformation of form, time and state, in fine or gross matter and in the organs.

sutras.en: A substance conforms itself to quiescent and uprisen and indeterminable external-aspects.
sutras.jn: Every object has its characteristics which are already quiescent, those which are active, and those which are not yet definable.
sutras.vv: That which is acted upon by transformations, either past, present, or yet to be manifested is the qualified.

sutras.en: The order of the sequence is the reason for the order of the mutations.
sutras.jn: Difference in stage is the cause of difference in development.
sutras.vv: The succession of changes is the cause of manifold evolution.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the three mutations [there follows] the knowledge of the past and the future.
sutras.jn: Through perfectly concentrated Meditation on the three stages of development comes a knowledge of past and future.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the three sorts of changes comes the knowledge of past and future.

sutras.en: Word and intended-object and presented-idea are confused because they are erroneously identified with each other. By constraint upon the distinctions between them [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of the cries of all living beings.
sutras.jn: The sound and the object and the thought called up by a word are confounded because they are all blurred together in the mind. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the distinction between them, there comes an understanding of the sounds uttered by all beings.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on word, meaning and knowledge, which are ordinarily confused, comes the knowledge of all animal sounds.

sutras.en: As a result of direct perception of subliminal-impressions there is [intuitive] knowledge of previous births.
sutras.jn: When the mind-impressions become visible, there comes an understanding of previous births.
sutras.vv: By perceiving the impressions, (comes) the knowledge of past life.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon a presented-idea [there arises intuitive] knowledge of the mind-stuff of another.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on mind-images is gained the understanding of the thoughts of others.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the signs in another's body, knowledge of his mind comes.

sutras.en: But [the intuitive knowledge of the mind-stuff of another] does not have that [idea] together with that upon which it depends [as its object], since that [upon which it depends] is not-in-the-field [of consciousness].
sutras.jn: But since that on which the thought in the mind of another rests is not objective to the thought-reader’s consciousness, he perceives the thought only, and not also that on which the thought rests.
sutras.vv: But not its contents, that not being the object of the Samyama.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the [outer] form of the body, when its power to be known is stopped, then as a consequence of the disjunction of the light and of the eye there follows indiscernibility [of the yogin's body].
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the form of the body, by arresting the body’s perceptibility, and by inhibiting the eye’s power of sight, there comes the power to make the body invisible.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the form of the body, the perceptibility of the form being obstructed and the power of manifestation in the eye being separated, the Yogi's body becomes unseen.

sutras.iast: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamād aparāntajñānam ariṣṭebhyo vā
sutras.deva: सोपक्रमं निरुपक्रमं च कर्म तत्संयमादपरान्तज्ञानमरिष्टेभ्यो वा
sutras.en: Advancing and not-advancing is karma; as a result of constraint upon this [twofold karma] or from the signs of death [there arises an intuitive] knowledge of the latter end.
sutras.jn: The works which fill out the life-span may be either immediately or gradually operative. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on these comes a knowledge of the time of the end, as also through signs.
sutras.vv: Karma is of two kinds — soon to be fructified and late to be fructified. By making Samyana on these, or by the signs called Arishta, portents, the Yogis know the exact time of separation from their bodies.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon friendliness and other [sentiments there arise] powers [of friendliness].
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on sympathy, compassion and kindness, is gained the power of interior union with others.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on friendship, mercy, etc. (I. 33 ), the Yogi excels in the respective qualities.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon powers [there arise] powers like those of an elephant.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on power, even such power as that of the elephant may be gained.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the strength of the elephant and others, their respective strength comes to the Yogi.

sutras.en: As a result of casting the light of a sense-activity [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of the subtile and the concealed and the obscure.
sutras.jn: By bending upon them the awakened inner light, there comes a knowledge of things subtle, or concealed, or obscure.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the Effulgent Light (I. 36 ), comes the knowledge of the fine, the obstructed, and the remote.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the sun [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of the cosmic-spaces.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the sun comes a knowledge of the worlds.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the sun, (comes) the knowledge of the world.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the moon [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of the arrangement of the stars.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the moon comes a knowledge of the lunar mansions.
sutras.vv: On the moon, (comes) the knowledge of the cluster of stars.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the pole-star [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of their movements.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the fixed pole-star comes a knowledge of the motions of the stars.
sutras.vv: On the pole-star, (comes) the knowledge of the motions of the stars.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the wheel of the navel [there arises the intuitive] knowledge of the arrangement of the body.
sutras.jn: Perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the lower trunk brings an understanding of the order of the bodily powers.
sutras.vv: On the navel circle, (comes) the knowledge of the constitution of the body.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the well of the throat [there follows] the cessation of hunger and thirst.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the well of the throat, there comes the cessation of hunger and thirst.
sutras.vv: On the hollow of the throat, (comes) cessation of hunger.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the tortoise-tube [there follows] motionlessness of the mind-stuff.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the centre of force in the channel called the “tortoise-formed,” comes steadfastness.
sutras.vv: On the nerve called Kurma, (comes) fixity of the body.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the radiance in the head [there follows] the sight of the Siddhas.
sutras.jn: Through perfectly concentrated Meditation on the light in the head comes the vision of the Masters who have attained.
sutras.vv: On the light emanating from the top of the head, sight of the Siddhas.

sutras.en: Or as a result of vividness the yogin discerns all.
sutras.jn: Or through the divining power of tuition he knows all things.
sutras.vv: Or by the power of Prâtibha, all knowledge.

sutras.en: [As a result of constraint] upon the heart [there arises] a consciousness of the mind-stuff.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation on the heart, the interior being, comes the knowledge of consciousness.
sutras.vv: In the heart, knowledge of minds.

sutras.iast: sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthāt svārthasaṃyamāt puruṣajñānam
sutras.en: Experience is a presented-idea which fails to distinguish the sattva and the Self, which are absolutely uncommingled [in the presented-idea]. Since the sattva exists as object for another, the [intuitive] knowledge of the Self arises as the result of constraint upon that which exists for its own sake.
sutras.jn: The personal self seeks to feast on life, through a failure to perceive the distinction between the personal self and the spiritual man. All personal experience really exists for the sake of another: namely, the spiritual man. By perfectly concentrated Meditation on experience for the sake of the Self, comes a knowledge of the spiritual man.
sutras.vv: Enjoyment comes from the non-discrimination of the soul and Sattva which are totally different because the latter's actions are for another. Samyama on the self-centred one gives knowledge of the Purusha.

sutras.en: As a result of this [constraint upon that which exists for its own sake], there arise vividness and the organ-of-[supernal]-hearing and the organ-of-[supernal]-touch and the organ-of-[supernal]-sight and the organ-of-[supernal]-taste and the organ-of-[supernal]-smell.
sutras.jn: Thereupon are born the divine power of intuition, and the hearing, the touch, the vision, the taste and the power of smell of the spiritual man.
sutras.vv: From that arises the knowledge belonging to Pratibha and (supernatural) hearing, touching, seeing, tasting and smelling.

sutras.en: In concentration these [supernal activities] are obstacles; in the emergent state they are perfections (siddhi).
sutras.jn: These powers stand in contradistinction to the highest spiritual vision. In manifestation they are called magical powers.
sutras.vv: These are obstacles to Samadhi; but they are powers in the worldly state.

sutras.en: As a result of slackening the causes of bondage and as a result of the knowledge of the procedure [of the mind-stuff], the mind-stuff penetrates into the body of another.
sutras.jn: Through the weakening of the causes of bondage, and by learning the method of sassing, the consciousness is transferred to the other body.
sutras.vv: When the cause of bondage of the Chitta has become loosened, the Yogi, by his knowledge of its channels of activity (the nerves), enters another's body.

sutras.en: As a result of mastering the Udāna there is no adhesion to water or mud or thorns or similar objects, and [at death] the upward flight.
sutras.jn: Through mastery of the upward-life comes freedom from the dangers of water, morass, and thorny places, and the power of ascension is gained.
sutras.vv: By conquering the current called Udâna the Yogi does not sink in water or in swamps, he can walk on thorns etc., and can, die at will.

sutras.en: As a result of mastering the Samāna [there arises] a radiance.
sutras.jn: By mastery of the binding-life comes radiance.
sutras.vv: By the conquest of the current Samâna he is surrounded by a blaze of light.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the relation between the organ-of-hearing and the air, [there arises] the supernal-organ-of-hearing.
sutras.jn: From perfectly concentrated Meditation on the correlation of hearing and the ether, comes the power of spiritual hearing.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the relation between the ear and the Akâsha comes divine hearing.

sutras.en: Either as a result of constraint upon the relation between the body and the air, or as a result of the balanced-state of lightness, such as that of cotton-fibre, there follows the passing through air.
sutras.jn: By perfectly concentrated Meditation em the correlation of the body with the ether, and by thinking of it as light as thistle-down, will come the power to traverse the ether.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the relation between the Akasha and the body and becoming light as cotton-wool etc., through meditation on them, the yogi goes through the skies.

sutras.iast: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ
sutras.en: An outwardly unadjusted fluctuation is the Great Discarnate; as a result of this the dwindling of the covering to the brightness.
sutras.jn: When that condition of consciousness is reached, which is far-reaching and not confined to the body, which is outside the body and not conditioned by it, then the veil which conceals the light is worn away.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the "real modifications" of the mind, outside of the body, called great disembodiedness, comes disappearance of the covering to light.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the coarse and the essential-attribute and the subtile and the inherence and purposiveness, there is a mastery of the elements.
sutras.jn: Mastery of the elements comes from perfectly concentrated Meditation on their five forms: the gross, the elemental, the subtle, the inherent, the purposive.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the gross and fine forms of the elements, their essential traits, the inherence of the Gunas in them and on their contributing to the experience of the soul, comes mastery of the elements.

sutras.en: As a result of this, atomization and the other [perfections] come about, [there is] perfection of body; and there is no obstruction by the properties of these [elements].
sutras.jn: Thereupon will come the manifestation of the atomic and other powers, which are the endowment of the body, together with its unassailable force.
sutras.vv: From that comes minuteness and the rest of the powers, "glorification of the body," and indestructibleness of the bodily qualities.

sutras.en: Beauty and grace and power and compactness of the thunderbolt, — [this is] perfection of body.
sutras.jn: Shapeliness, beauty, force, the temper of the diamond: these are the endowments of that body.
sutras.vv: The "glorification of the body" is beauty, complexion, strength, adamantine hardness.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon the process-of-knowing and the essential-attribute and the feeling-of-personality and the inherence and the purposiveness, [there follows] the subjugation of the organs.
sutras.jn: Mastery over the powers of perception and action comes through perfectly concentrated Meditation on their fivefold forms; namely, their power to grasp their distinctive nature, the element of self-consciousness in them, their inherence, and their purposiveness.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the objectivity and power of illumination of the organs, on egoism, the inherence of the Gunas in them and on their contributing to the experience of the soul, comes the conquest of the organs.

sutras.en: As a result of this [there follows] speed [great as that] of the central-organ, action of the instruments [of knowledge] disjunct [from the body], and the subjugation of the primary-cause.
sutras.jn: Thence comes the power swift as thought, independent of instruments, and the mastery over matter.
sutras.vv: From that comes to the body the power of rapid movement like the mind, power of the organs independently of the body, and conquest of nature.

sutras.en: He who has only the full discernment into the difference between the sattva and the Self is one who has authority over all states-of-existence and is one who knows all.
sutras.jn: When the spiritual man is perfectly disentangled from the psychic body, he attains to mastery over all things and to a knowledge of all.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on the discrimination between the Sattva and the Purusha come omnipotence and omniscience.

sutras.en: As a result of passionlessness even with regard to these [perfections] there follows, after the dwindling of the seeds of the defects, Isolation.
sutras.jn: By absence of all self-indulgence at this point, when the seeds of bondage to sorrow are destroyed, pure spiritual being is attained.
sutras.vv: By giving up even these powers comes the destruction of the very seed of evil, which leads to Kaivalya.

sutras.en: In case of invitations from those-in-high-places, these should arouse no attachment or pride, for undesired consequences recur.
sutras.jn: There should be complete overcoming of allurement or pride in the invitations of the different realms of life, lest attachment to things evil arise once more.
sutras.vv: The Yogi should not feel allured or flattered by the overtures of celestial beings for fear of evil again.

sutras.en: As a result of constraint upon moments and their sequence [there arises the intuitive] knowledge proceeding from discrimination.
sutras.jn: From perfectly concentrated Meditation on the divisions of time and their succession comes that wisdom which is born of discernment.
sutras.vv: By making Samyama on a particle of time and its precession and succession comes discrimination.

sutras.en: As a result of this there arises the deeper-knowledge of two equivalent things which cannot be distinctly qualified in species or characteristic-mark or point-of-space.
sutras.jn: Hence comes discernment between things which are of like nature, not distinguished by difference of kind, character or position.
sutras.vv: Those things which cannot be differentiated by species, sign, and place, even they will be discriminated by the above Samyama.

sutras.iast: tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam
sutras.deva: तारकं सर्वविषयं सर्वथाविषयमक्रमं चेति विवेकजं ज्ञानम्
sutras.en: The [intuitive] knowledge proceeding from discrimination is a deliverer, has all things as its object, and has all times for its object, and is an [inclusive whole] without sequence.
sutras.jn: The wisdom which is born of discernment is starlike; it discerns all things, and all conditions of things, it discerns without succession: simultaneously.
sutras.vv: The saving knowledge is that knowledge of discrimination which simultaneously covers all objects, in all their variations.

sutras.en: When the purity of the sattva and of the Self are equal there is Isolation.
sutras.jn: When the vesture and the spiritual man are alike pure, then perfect spiritual life is attained.
sutras.vv: By the similarity of purity between the Sattva and the Purusha comes Kaivalya.

sutras.en: Perfections proceed from birth or from drugs or from spells or from self-castigation or from concentration.
sutras.jn: Psychic and spiritual powers may be inborn, or they may be gained by the use of drugs, or by incantations, or by fervour, or by Meditation.
sutras.vv: The Siddhis (powers) are attained by birth, chemical means, power of words, mortification, or concentration.

sutras.en: The mutation into another birth is the result of the filling in of the evolving-cause.
sutras.jn: The transfer of powers from one venture to another comes through the flow of the natural creative forces.
sutras.vv: The change into another species is by the filling in of nature.

sutras.iast: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat
sutras.en: The efficient cause gives no impulse to the evolving-causes but [the mutation] follows when the barrier [to the evolving-cause] is cut, as happens with the peasant.
sutras.jn: The apparent, immediate cause is not the true cause of the creative nature-powers; but, like the husbandman in his field, it takes obstacles away.
sutras.vv: Good and bad deeds are not the direct causes in the transformations of nature, but they act as breakers of obstacles to the evolutions of nature: as a farmer breaks the obstacles to the course of water, which then runs down by its own nature.

sutras.en: Created mind-stuffs may result from the sense-of-personality and from this alone.
sutras.jn: Vestures of consciousness are built up in conformity with the Boston of the feeling of selfhood.
sutras.vv: From egoism alone proceed the created minds.
sutras.jnote: Gutenberg prints “the Boston of the feeling of selfhood”, which looks like a transcription error. Not yet checked against the 1912 printing.

sutras.en: While there is a variety of actions, the mind-stuff which impels the many is one.
sutras.jn: In the different fields of manifestation, the Consciousness, though one, is the elective cause of many states of consciousness.
sutras.vv: Though the activities of the different created minds are various, the one original mind is the controller of them all.

sutras.en: Of these [five perfections] that which proceeds from contemplation leaves no latent-deposit.
sutras.jn: Among states of consciousness, that which is born of Contemplation is free from the seed of future sorrow.
sutras.vv: Among the various Chittas, that which is attained by Samadhi is desireless.

sutras.en: The yogin's karma is neither-white-nor-black; [the karma] of others is of three kinds.
sutras.jn: The works of followers after Union make neither for bright pleasure nor for dark pain The works of others make for pleasure or pain, or a mingling of these.
sutras.vv: Works are neither black nor white for the Yogis; for others they are threefold — black, white, and mixed.

sutras.en: As a result of this there follows the manifestation of those subconscious-impressions only which correspond to the fruition of their [karma].
sutras.jn: From the force inherent in works comes the manifestation of those dynamic mind images which are conformable to the ripening out of each of these works.
sutras.vv: From these threefold works are manifested in each state only those desires (which are) fitting to that state alone. (The others are held in abeyance for the time being.)

sutras.en: There is an uninterrupted-causal-relation [of subconscious-impressions], although remote in species and point-of-space and moment-of-time, by reason of the correspondence between memory and subliminal-impressions.
sutras.jn: Works separated by different nature, or place, or time, are brought together by the correspondence between memory and dynamic impression.
sutras.vv: There is consecutiveness in desires, even though separated by species, space, and time, there being identification of memory and impressions.

sutras.en: Furthermore the [subconscious-impressions] have no beginning [that we can set in time], since desire is permanent.
sutras.jn: The series of dynamic mind-images is beginningless, because Desire is everlasting.
sutras.vv: Thirst for happiness being eternal, desires are without beginning.

sutras.en: Since [subconscious-impressions] are associated with cause and motive and mental-substrate and stimulus, if these cease to be, then those [subconscious-impressions] cease to be.
sutras.jn: Since the dynamic mind-images are held together by impulses of desire, by the wish for personal reward, by the substratum of mental habit, by the support of outer things desired; therefore, when these cease, the self reproduction of dynamic mind-images ceases.
sutras.vv: Being held together by cause, effect, support, and objects, in the absence of these is its absence.

sutras.en: Past and future as such exist; [therefore subconscious-impressions do not cease to be]. For the different time-forms belong to the external-aspects.
sutras.jn: The difference between that which is past and that which is not yet come, according to their natures, depends on the difference of phase of their properties.
sutras.vv: The past and future exist in their own nature, qualities having different ways.

sutras.en: These [external-aspects with the three time-forms] are phenomenalized [individuals] or subtile [generic-forms] and their essence is the aspects (guṇa).
sutras.jn: These properties, whether manifest or latent, are of the nature of the Three Potencies.
sutras.vv: They are manifested or fine, being of the nature of the Gunas.

sutras.en: The that-ness of a thing is due to a singleness of mutation.
sutras.jn: The external manifestation of an object takes place when the transformations ore in the same phase.
sutras.vv: The unity in things is from the unity in changes.

sutras.en: Because, while the [physical] thing remains the same, the mind-stuffs are different, [therefore the two are upon] distinct levels-of-existence.
sutras.jn: The paths of material things and of states of consciousness are distinct, as is manifest from the fact that the same object may produce different impressions in different minds.
sutras.vv: Since perception and desire vary with regard to the same object, mind and object are of different nature.

sutras.iast: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt
sutras.deva: न चैकचित्ततन्त्रं वस्तु तदप्रमाणकं तदा किं स्यात्
sutras.en: And a thing is not dependent upon a single mind-stuff, [for then in certain cases] it could not be proved [by that mind-stuff], [and] then what would it be?
sutras.jn: Nor do material objects depend upon a single mind, for how could they remain objective to others, if that mind ceased to think of them?

sutras.en: A thing is known or not known by virtue of its affecting [or not affecting] the mind-stuff.
sutras.jn: An object is perceived, or not perceived, according as the mind is, or is not, tinged with the colour of the object.
sutras.vv: Things are known or unknown to the mind, being dependent on the colouring which they give to the mind.

sutras.en: Unintermittently the Master of that [mind-stuff] knows the fluctuations of mind-stuff [and thus] the Self undergoes-no-mutations.
sutras.jn: The movements of the psychic nature are perpetually objects of perception, since the Spiritual Man, who is the lord of them, remains unchanging.
sutras.vv: The states of the mind are always known, because the lord of the mind, the Purusha, is unchangeable.

sutras.en: It does not illumine itself, since it is an object-for-sight.
sutras.jn: The Mind is not self-luminous, since it can be seen as an object.
sutras.vv: The mind is not self-luminous, being an object.

sutras.en: And there cannot be a cognition of both [thinking-substance and thing] at the same time.
sutras.jn: Nor could the Mind at the same time know itself and things external to it.
sutras.vv: From its being unable to cognise both at the same time.

sutras.en: If [one mind-stuff] were the object-for-sight for another, there would be an infinite regress from one thinking-substance to another thinking-substance as well as confusion of memory.
sutras.jn: If the Mind be thought of as seen by another more inward Mind, then there would be an endless series of perceiving Minds, and a confusion of memories.
sutras.vv: Another cognising mind being assumed, there will be no end to such assumptions, and confusion of memory will be the result.
