sutras.en: The Intellect (citi) which unites not [with objects] is conscious of its own thinking-substance when [the mind-stuff] takes the form of that [thinking-substance by reflecting it].
sutras.jn: When the psychical nature takes on the form of the spiritual intelligence, by reflecting it, then the Self becomes conscious of its own spiritual intelligence.
sutras.vv: The essence of knowledge (the Purusha) being unchangeable, when the mind takes its form, it becomes conscious.

sutras.en: Mind-stuff affected by the Seer and by the object-for-sight [leads to the perception of] all intended-objects.
sutras.jn: The psychic nature, taking on the colour of the Seer and of things seen, leads to the perception of all objects.
sutras.vv: Coloured by the seer and the seen the mind is able to understand everything.

sutras.iast: tad asaṃkhyeyavāsanābhiś citram api parārthaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt
sutras.en: This [mind-stuff], although diversified by countless subconscious-impressions, exists for the sake of another, because its nature is to produce [things as] combinations.
sutras.jn: The psychic nature, which has been printed with mind-images of innumerable material things, exists now for the Spiritual Man, building for him.
sutras.vv: The mind, though variegated by innumerable desires, acts for another (the Purusha), because it acts in combination.

sutras.en: For him who sees the distinction, pondering upon his own states-of-being ceases.
sutras.jn: For him who discerns between the Mind and the Spiritual Man, there comes perfect fruition of the longing after the real being of the Self.
sutras.vv: For the discriminating, the perception of the mind as Atman ceases.

sutras.en: Then the mind-stuff is borne down to discrimination, onward towards Isolation.
sutras.jn: Thereafter, the whole personal being bends toward illumination, toward Eternal Life.
sutras.vv: Then, bent on discriminating, the mind attains the previous state of Kaivalya (isolation). (There is another reading — कैवल्यप्राग्भारं।  The meaning then would be: "Then the mind becomes deep in discrimination and gravitates towards Kaivalya." — Ed.)

sutras.en: In the intervals of this [mind-stuff] there are other presented-ideas [coming] from subliminal-impressions.
sutras.jn: In the internals of the batik, other thoughts will arise, through the impressions of the dynamic mind-images.
sutras.vv: The thoughts that arise as obstructions to that are from impressions.

sutras.en: The escape from these [subliminal-impressions] is described as being like [the escape from] the hindrances.
sutras.jn: These are to be overcome as it was taught that hindrances should be overcome.
sutras.vv: Their destruction is in the same manner as of ignorance, egoism, etc., as said before (II. 10).

sutras.iast: prasaṃkhyāne 'py akusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāter dharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ
sutras.en: For one who is not usurious even in respect of Elevation, there follows in every case as a result of discriminative discernment the concentration [called] Rain-cloud of [knowable] things.
sutras.jn: He who, after he has attained, is wholly free from self, reaches the essence of all that can be known, gathered together like a cloud. This is the true spiritual consciousness.
sutras.vv: Even when arriving at the right discriminating knowledge of the essences, he who gives up the fruits, unto him comes, as the result of perfect domination, the Samadhi called the cloud of virtue.

sutras.en: Then follows the cessation of the hindrances and of karma.
sutras.jn: Thereon comes surcease from sorrow and the burden of toil.
sutras.vv: From that comes cessation of pain and works.

sutras.en: Then, because of the endlessness of knowledge from which all obscuring defilements have passed away, what is yet to be known amounts to little.
sutras.jn: When all veils are rent, all stains washed away, his knowledge becomes infinite; little remains for him to know.
sutras.vv: The knowledge, bereft of covering and impurities, becoming infinite, the knowable becomes small.

sutras.en: When as a result of this the aspects (guṇa) have fulfilled their purpose, they attain to the limit of the sequence of mutations.
sutras.jn: Thereafter comes the completion of the series of transformations of the three nature potencies, since their purpose is attained.
sutras.vv: Then are finished the successive transformations of the qualities, they having attained the end.

sutras.en: The positive correlate to the moment, recognized as such at the final limit of the mutation, is a sequence.
sutras.jn: The series of transformations is divided into moments. When the series is completed, time gives place to duration.
sutras.vv: The changes that exist in relation to moments and which are perceived at the other end (at the end of a series) are succession.

sutras.iast: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti
sutras.deva: पुरुषार्थशून्यानां गुणानां प्रतिप्रसवः कैवल्यं स्वरूपप्रतिष्ठा वा चितिशक्तिरिति
sutras.en: Isolation is the inverse generation of the aspects, no longer provided with a purpose by the Self, or it is the Energy of Intellect grounded in itself.
sutras.jn: Pure spiritual life is, therefore, the inverse resolution of the potencies of Nature, which have emptied themselves of their value for the Spiritual man; or it is the return of the power of pure Consciousness to its essential form.
sutras.vv: The resolution in the inverse order of the qualities, bereft of any motive of action for the Purusha, is Kaivalya, or it is the establishment of the power of knowledge in its own nature.

concepts.gloss: The field of awareness that takes the shape of whatever it attends to; what yoga sets out to still.
A movement or modification of the mind. The text names five kinds.
The restraint or settling of the mind's fluctuations; the text's own definition of yoga (1.2).
Sustained, repeated effort toward steadiness; one of the two means paired in 1.12.
Freedom from craving for what is seen or heard of; the partner of practice.
A special Self untouched by hindrance or karma; devotion to it is one path to concentration.
The sacred syllable that expresses Īśvara (1.27).
The five root troubles of the mind, listed in 2.3.
Taking the impermanent, impure, painful and not-self for their opposites (2.5); the root of the other afflictions.
Mistaking the power of seeing for the instrument of seeing as one self (2.6).
Pain and dissatisfaction. Future suffering is what yoga sets out to avoid (2.16).
Action and the residue it leaves, ripening as birth, lifespan and experience.
A latent trace left in the mind by experience, which shapes later activity.
A stored tendency waiting for the conditions that will express it.
Pure consciousness, the witness, distinct from everything it sees.
The one who sees; another name for puruṣa.
Everything that can be an object of awareness, made of the three guṇas.
The three strands of nature: brightness, activity and inertia.
Primary matter, the source from which the seen world evolves.
The content held in the mind at a given moment.
Memory, one of the five fluctuations; also mindfulness in 1.20.
Knowledge carried by words with no real object behind it (1.9).
The mind as the organ that coordinates the senses.
The mind resting on a single object.
Direct wisdom arising from concentration.
Discriminating the seer from the seen; the means of release (2.26).
The mind taking on the colour of its object, like a clear jewel (1.41).
Seed: concentration with a seed has an object; seedless concentration has none.
Complete absorption in the object; the eighth limb and the subject of the first pāda.
Extraordinary powers, called obstacles to concentration in 3.37.
Aloneness: the Self standing in its own nature, free of the seen.
Change of form, state or time in the mind and in things.
The first limb: non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, non-grasping.
The second limb: cleanliness, contentment, discipline, study, devotion.
The third limb: a seat that is steady and easy (2.46).
The fourth limb: regulating the movement of breath.
The fifth limb: the senses turning from their objects.
The sixth limb: binding the mind to one place.
The seventh limb: an unbroken flow of attention toward the object.
Focus, meditation and absorption practised together on one object.
The first restraint; enmity falls away in its presence (2.35).
Austerity or disciplined effort; part of kriyā-yoga and the observances.
Study and recitation; part of kriyā-yoga and the observances.
Friendliness toward the happy; one of four attitudes that clear the mind (1.33).
